_about: One decision per pipeline. Set start_by to schedule or event_trigger, then fill in only that part and leave the other one as it is. A schedule takes frequency (minute, hourly, daily, weekly or monthly), interval (for minute and hourly), days (for weekly, in week order starting with Monday), times (24-hour, earliest first) and end. Use the simplest frequency that fits. A trigger takes source (azure_blob_events or onelake_events), event_types, folder and the parameters it passes to the pipeline. All times are UTC.

price_feed.needs: Load supplier prices every 30 minutes, around the clock, every day.

store_close.needs: Load store sales at 07:00 and 13:00 on Monday to Friday. Never at the weekend.

nightly_rebuild.needs: Rebuild the gold tables every night at 01:00 for the foreseeable future. The team's rule is that a schedule with no planned end ends on 2099-12-31.

partner_drop.needs: A partner writes .csv files into the orders folder of its Azure Blob Storage container. Load each new or overwritten file as soon as it lands. A deleted file must not start a run.

lake_landing.needs: Files land in the inbound folder of the Landing lakehouse in OneLake. Start a load for each new file and pass its name in the pipeline parameter file_name. The team also tests the pipeline by running it by hand.

lake_cleanup.needs: When a file is deleted from the inbound folder of the Landing lakehouse, remove its row from the file log at once.
